Forecast Discussion

A cold front moved through early this morning, and we are now in a drier, cooler NW flow.

An upper-level low over the Great Lakes and eastern Canada is carving a trough in the eastern US early this week. Cooler and drier air is streaming into the Southern Appalachians in the counterclockwise flow around that low. Surface high pressure settles in south of the upper-level low and into the Central Appalachians, making skies mostly sunny through Tuesday. The trough holds the door open for another front to sweep through from the northwest Thursday. It will not have the chilly air in tow, however.

Monday and Tuesday look mighty fine with cool nights.

Today's front sneaks back to the north midweek ahead of Thursday's front. Expect isolated showers and thundershowers Wednesday afternoon and evening along with slightly warmer temperatures. Thursday afternoon is the wettest period of the week in a squeeze play between the two fronts.

Computer guidance differs somewhat about how cleanly the front will move through. So, I held the door open for an isolated afternoon shower or thundershower Friday, and I could not completely rule out a stray shower or thundershower Saturday afternoon. Temperatures creep back up by Saturday.
